admission_shapes.table: 3x8 admitted; 4x6 admitted; 2x12 admitted; 6x4 REFUSED; 12x2 REFUSED; 24x1 REFUSED — 'only 5 concurrent phase jobs fit'

admission_shapes.consequence: The worker-scaling route is memory-capped at 5 concurrent jobs, giving at most 5/3 x barrier reduction, not the ideal 8x CPU-filling the Astra table sketched.

derived_floors.svf_phase_amdahl_twin_only: r_G = 1/(0.667+0.333/4.126) = 1.265x -> chain ~5756 s = 95.9 min = 1.149x overall (whole-tile measured ratio 1.679 agrees)
derived_floors.barrier_worker_scaling_only: 5 workers -> barrier ~816 s -> phase ~3546 s -> chain ~86.4 min = 1.275x overall (ideal-scaling projection, to be measured in P1c)
derived_floors.twin_plus_5_workers: barrier ~312-504 s, export loop unchanged -> phase ~3042-3234 s -> chain ~82-84.5 min = 1.30-1.34x overall (projection)
derived_floors.export_loop_concurrency_ceiling: export loop 2729.7 s at 5-way concurrency -> ~546 s -> phase ~858 s with twin+5 workers -> chain ~54.7 min = ~2.0x overall (upper-bound projection; export parallelism is a scheduling change requiring its own protocol, exactness argument, and review)
derived_floors.caveat: All projections are Amdahl arithmetic on measured segments, not measurements. Barrier scaling may be sub-ideal (memory bandwidth, admission interplay); P1c measures it.
